findings.rule: Composition root is the only place that wires concretes (dependency inversion)
findings.explanation: The application-layer service imports and instantiates the concrete infrastructure adapter FsArchiveStore instead of depending on the ArchiveStore port already defined in vendor/shared/adapters.ts. Only platform/container.ts may construct concrete adapters; a service must reach external I/O through a container-provided port.
findings.fix: Constructor-inject `archive: ArchiveStore` into ExportsService and construct FsArchiveStore in the container (with an override slot, like the other adapters), wiring it into the exports service there.

findings.rule: Configuration/environment access belongs to the composition root
findings.explanation: The service reads process.env (ARCHIVE_DIR, EXPORT_SIGNING_SECRET) directly. In this project all config is loaded once at the composition root (platform/config via loadConfig, secrets via SecretsProvider) and injected; no module code touches the environment.
findings.fix: Move both values into AppConfig (or SecretsProvider for the signing secret) and pass them to FsArchiveStore where it is constructed in the container.

findings.rule: Port interfaces belong in the domain layer (vendor/shared), not in infrastructure
findings.explanation: The Clock port is declared inside the adapters directory, so the application layer (service.ts:1) and the container import the port type from infrastructure — the service's source dependency points outward instead of inward to vendor/shared, where all other adapter interfaces (LLMProvider, GitHubClient, SecretsProvider, ArchiveStore) live.
findings.fix: Move `interface Clock` into server/src/vendor/shared/adapters.ts and have SystemClock in adapters/clock implement it; service and container then import the Clock type from vendor/shared.
